core.title: Make every user/system flow structurally valid
core.given: A user/system flow definition or registry entry is in scope for the plan (new or existing).
core.when: The planner authors, edits, reviews or validates that user/system flow, whatever field is touched.
core.then: The user/system flow passes all seven structural validation checks: typed user/system flow id in the profiled user/system flow URN shape, category declared as a field, the declared spec artifact exists, participants declared, valid dependencies, sequence artifacts named in the profiled artifact-reference form, themes declared.
prefer: Write the user/system flow id in the stack's typed user/system flow URN shape.
Declare the user/system flow's category in its own field with one of nominal|error|alternate|exception.
Make sure a spec artifact exists at the user/system flow's declared location (create it or fix the declared location).
List every participant the user/system flow uses in its participants list.
Point every dependency at an existing, valid user/system flow id.
Name every artifact in the user/system flow's sequence in the plan's artifact-reference form.
Declare every theme the user/system flow uses in its themes list.
avoid: Untyped or free-form user/system flow ids that do not match the profiled user/system flow URN shape.
Encoding the category as a digit inside the user/system flow identity.
Declaring a spec location that has no artifact behind it.
Using participants, themes or dependencies that are not declared / do not resolve.
Sequence artifacts not in the profiled artifact-reference form.
Treating any of the seven checks as optional or advisory.
core.why: User/system flows are consumed mechanically by the registry and validators; a user/system flow that breaks any structural rule cannot be addressed, resolved or checked reliably.
evidence: User/system flow id matches the profiled user/system flow URN shape.
No digit-encoded category in the identity; category field present with value in {nominal, error, alternate, exception}.
A spec artifact exists at the user/system flow's declared location.
Every participant referenced is in the participants list.
Every dependency resolves to a valid user/system flow id.
Every sequence artifact matches the profiled artifact-reference form.
Every theme used is declared in the themes list.
verification: Strict disposition: a user/system flow fails if any one of the seven structural checks fails; none of the checks is optional or advisory.
The check applies to every in-scope user/system flow, including existing unchanged user/system flows; it is not gated on a field-level diff.
The spec-artifact existence check relies on the user/system flow registry convention, which must enforce spec-file existence.
Activation signal precedence: task-term matches alone do not prove user/system-flow-authoring intent; the file-kind signal (user/system flow definition or registry entry) is primary.

values: existing user/system flow in scope for validation

fires: Planner creates a new user/system flow definition or registry entry.
Planner edits any field of an existing user/system flow (id, category, spec location, participants, dependencies, sequence, themes, or prose) while the user/system flow is in scope.
Planner reviews or validates existing user/system flows in the plan, even without changing them.
doesNotFire: Edits to product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES or acceptances when no user/system flow definition or registry entry is in scope.
Code or test changes unrelated to plan artifacts.

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape a user/system flow's typed id must match; the core's id check, prefer and evidence are expressed against this shape.
The reference form every artifact entry in a user/system flow's sequence must match (short domain-and-resource reference, distinct from the artifact's full URN).

bunOnly.text: Spec-file existence check relies on planner.user-system-flow.registry (requires edge: validation enforces spec-file existence).
bunOnly.reason: Names the concrete ATDD-Bun rule id and its graph edge; the core states the dependency generically (the user/system flow registry convention enforces spec-file existence), and the specific cross-rule wiring is a realization detail.

neutralityNotes: User/system flows, the user/system flow registry, DESIRED OUTCOMES and product capabilities are treated as stack-neutral ATDD plan-model vocabulary (the closed profile vocabulary itself recognizes user-system-flow/desired-outcome/capability as URN artifacts), so the seven checks, the category vocabulary nominal|error|alternate|exception and the activation kinds/terms stay in the core. The only concrete syntaxes were pushed to the profile: the user/system flow id shape via urn.user-system-flow, and the sequence-artifact reference form via the proposed urn.grammar#user_system_flow_sequence_artifact (no existing key fits; it is a short reference, not a full URN, a binding, or a self-declaration). The cross-rule dependency on the user/system-flow-registry convention is stated generically in core.verification; the ATDD-Bun rule id planner.user-system-flow.registry and its graph edge remain bunOnly. Core activation facts drop the per-fact notes (the core fact schema has no note field); their semantics are preserved in the verification array (scope and signal precedence).
